rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghayth is rain, al-kuffar means cultivators, yahīj describes movement or growth, and al-hutam is brittle, broken dry vegetation.
rows.anchor: والغيث المطر والكفار جمع كافر بمعنى الحارث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life resembles rain whose attractive crop grows to its fullest, yellows, then breaks apart and is scattered by winds.
rows.anchor: مثل الحياة الدنيا في بهجتها المعجبة ثم الزوال كمثل مطر أعجب الحراث نباته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness precedes divine approval because cleansing the place of sins prepares it to receive approval; calling forgiveness from God hints it is the primary aim, while punishment follows human departure from servitude.
rows.anchor: سبق المغفرة على الرضوان لتطهير المحل ليحل به الرضوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly life is a pleasure whose enjoyment deludes the person attached to it; the afterlife contrast warns hearers to choose forgiveness and approval over punishment.
rows.anchor: أي متاع التمتع منه هو الغرور به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing warning awakens people so worldly life, especially its delusive attractions, will not deceive them.
rows.anchor: تنبيه وإيقاظ لئلا تغره الحياة الدنيا بخاصة غروره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Racing toward forgiveness requires more than hastening: each person strives to move faster than a rival, whereas hastening only means increasing one's own pace.
rows.anchor: ففي معنى المسابقة ما يزيد على معنى المسارعة فإن المسارعة الجد في تسريع الحركة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some distinguish the promise in 3:133 as a paradise for those brought near, wider than the paradise promised here to ordinary believers, citing the different descriptions of its width.
rows.anchor: ما قيل إن آية آل عمران في السابقين المقربين والآية التي نحن فيها في عامة المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That distinction is unsound because this verse commands an even greater effort than 3:133, and the generic singular heaven here corresponds to the plural heavens there.
rows.anchor: وجه عدم الاستقامة ما عرفت أن المكلف به في الآية المبحوث عنها معنى فوق ما كلف به في آية آل عمران

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgiveness comes before paradise because life in paradise is pure, so entry requires removal of sins and their stains.
rows.anchor: وتقديم المغفرة على الجنة في الآية لأن الحياة في الجنة حياة طاهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised paradise's width means its vast extent, not width opposed to length; the wording indicates immense breadth.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالعرض السعة دون العرض المقابل للطول وهو معنى شائع

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes width literally and says naming the shorter dimension alone is more emphatic: if it equals heaven and earth, its length is greater still.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالعرض ما يقابل الطول والاقتصار على ذكر العرض أبلغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concludes the chapter's account of Banu al-Nadir's breach and worldly and otherworldly loss, compounded by hypocrites urging opposition to God and His Messenger; their root failure was forgetting God and thereby losing sight of their own good.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة السبب في ذلك أنهم لم يراقبوا الله في أعمالهم ونسوه فأنساهم أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers should remember God and examine what they have sent ahead for the return and judgment, since deeds are preserved and bring an inescapable recompense.
rows.anchor: وينظر فيما يقدمه من العمل ليوم الرجوع إلى ربه فإن ما عمله محفوظ عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse calls for ongoing watchfulness that deeds be sound and sincere, followed by self-accounting: thank God for good, rebuke oneself for sins, and seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: يراقبوا أعمالهم أن تكون صالحة خالصة لوجهه الكريم مراقبة مستمرة ثم يحاسبوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Remembering God through the beautiful names and attributes taught in the Quran is the sole path to complete servitude, the highest human perfection.
rows.anchor: هو السبيل الوحيد الذي ينتهي بسالكه إلى كمال العبودية ولا كمال للإنسان فوقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A human is wholly owned by God and has no independent aspect; perfection means recognizing this dependence, embodying humility and need, and acting according to God's will without heedlessness.
rows.anchor: فكمال الإنسان في أن يرى نفسه مملوكا لله من غير استقلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only inward awareness of God, who witnesses and encompasses everything, lets a person view self, attributes, and actions as wholly dependent; then the heart finds reassurance.
rows.anchor: إلا مع التوجه الباطني إلى ربه الذي هو على كل شيء شهيد وبكل شيء محيط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author links the coming return to God with 70:6–7, where people regard it as distant while God sees it as near.
rows.anchor: إنهم يرونه بعيدا ونراه قريبا المعارج 6-7

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first command to fear God means obeying all commands and avoiding all prohibitions; each person should inspect what deeds are being presented for judgment and whether good deeds are accepted.
rows.anchor: اتقوا الله بطاعته في جميع ما يأمركم به وينهاكم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command concerns care within deeds already performed: repair them, make them sincere for God, and protect them from corruption; the first command governs doing deeds, the second their quality.
rows.anchor: ومن هنا تبين أن المراد بالتقوى في الموضعين مختلف

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the first command is repentance for past sins and the second avoidance of future sins; the author rejects this distinction.
rows.anchor: قول بعضهم إن الأولى للتوبة عما مضى من الذنوب والثانية لاتقاء المعاصي في المستقبل غير سديد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations make the first command about fulfilling obligations and the second about avoiding prohibitions, or treat the second as mere emphasis; the author rejects both.
rows.anchor: ومثله ما قيل إن الأمر الثاني لتأكيد الأمر الأول فحسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nisyān literally means a known representation leaving the mind after it had been present, with its source also lost; by extension it means turning away from something by failing to act on it.
rows.anchor: النسيان زوال صورة المعلوم عن النفس بعد حصولها فيها مع زوال مبدئه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extended sense of forgetting as neglect is illustrated by the warning that God will leave people as they neglected the meeting of that day.
rows.anchor: وقيل اليوم ننساكم كما نسيتم لقاء يومكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about those who forgot God reinforces the preceding call: send righteous deeds ahead for judgment, deeds through which the self truly lives.
rows.anchor: والآية بحسب لب معناها كالتأكيد لمضمون الآية السابقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forgetting oneself follows from forgetting God: people then imagine they exist independently, own their knowledge and power, and rely on outward causes instead of their Lord.
rows.anchor: إذ بنسيانه تعالى تنسى أسماؤه الحسنى وصفاته العليا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imagined independent self is not the real human being, who is wholly dependent, ignorant, helpless, lowly, and poor; every perfection belongs to and ends with God.
rows.anchor: بل الإنسان موجود متعلق الوجود جهل كله عجز كله ذلة كله فقر كله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because forgetting oneself is caused by forgetting God, the verse prohibits the cause rather than merely its effect; this is stronger and more persuasive than a direct general prohibition.
rows.anchor: حول النهي عن نسيان النفس في الآية إلى النهي عن نسيانه تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning alludes to the previously mentioned Jews of Banu al-Nadir and Banu Qaynuqa and others who opposed God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: من تقدم ذكرهم من يهود بني النضير وبني قينقاع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is also characterized as mighty and wise, as in 41:41 and 36:2.
rows.anchor: وقد وصف القرآن أيضا بالعزة والحكمة كما قال وإنه لكتاب عزيز

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar explains the unseen as what has not yet occurred and the witnessed as what has already occurred; the author calls this an interpretation through some instances only.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال الغيب ما لم يكن والشهادة ما قد كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report defining unseen and witnessed by what is yet to be and what has occurred gives examples of the terms rather than an exhaustive definition.
rows.anchor: أقول وهو تفسير ببعض المصاديق

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says God was living without an additional life, sovereign and powerful before creating anything, and a mighty king after creation.
rows.anchor: عن أبي بصير عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام في حديث لم يزل حيا بلا حياة وملكا قادرا قبل أن ينشىء شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's life is not an attribute added to God's essence; describing Him as king before creation refers the action-attribute of sovereignty back to essential power.
rows.anchor: أي بلا حياة زائدة على الذات

rows.speaker: هشام الجواليقي
rows.claim: When Hisham asked Abu Abdillah what saying Subhan Allah means, the Imam answered that it means declaring God transcendent.
rows.anchor: عن هشام الجواليقي قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: نهج البلاغة
rows.claim: Nahj al-Balagha describes God as Creator without motion or exertion.
rows.anchor: وفي نهج البلاغة والخالق لا بمعنى حركة ونصب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: A well-known prophetic saying urges people to account for themselves before being held to account, weigh themselves before being weighed, and prepare for the great presentation.
rows.anchor: وفي النبوي المشهور حاسبوا أنفسكم قبل أن تحاسبوا وزنوا قبل أن توزنوا

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الماضي عليه السلام
rows.claim: A daily self-accounting report says that whoever does good should increase gratitude to God, and whoever does evil should seek God's forgiveness and repent.
rows.anchor: إلى أبي الحسن الماضي عليه السلام قال ليس منا من لم يحاسب نفسه في كل يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author points readers to earlier reports on remembering God, including those discussed under 2:152 and 33:41.
rows.anchor: وقد أوردنا روايات عنهم عليهم السلام في معنى ذكر الله في ذيل تفسير قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns believers away from traits that cause hypocrisy, especially distraction by wealth and children and miserliness.
rows.anchor: تنبيه للمؤمنين أن يتجنبوا عن بعض الصفات التي تورث النفاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ilhāʾ means occupying or distracting; wealth and children distract when attachment to them as worldly adornment turns the heart away from God.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإلهاء الأموال والأولاد عن ذكر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Attachment empties the heart of remembrance, leaving only verbal profession without action or inward belief; when servants forget God, He forgets them, bringing clear loss.
rows.anchor: فلا يبقى له إلا القول من غير عمل وتصديق قلبي ونسيان العبد لربه يستعقب نسيانه تعالى له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loss is like the hypocrites who traded guidance for error and gained nothing; the author links this to 2:16.
rows.anchor: أولئك الذين اشتروا الضلالة بالهدى فما ربحت تجارتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse indirectly but emphatically forbids attachment: instead of merely warning believers not to be distracted, it treats wealth and children as having a distracting nature.
rows.anchor: والأصل هو نهي المؤمنين عن التلهي بالأموال والأولاد وتبديله من نهي الأموال والأولاد عن إلهائهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending covers every kind of charitable good, obligatory such as alms and expiations and voluntary; the wording reminds people that wealth is God's gift and remains His even when entrusted to them.
rows.anchor: للإشعار بأن أمره لهذا ليس سؤالا لما يملكونه دونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending before death means before the period of being able to use one's wealth in God's path ends.
rows.anchor: أي فينقطع أمد استطاعته من التصرف في ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dying person's request for a near extension implies contentment with only enough extra time to give charity, making the request easier; every future term is near.
rows.anchor: وهو مقدار ما يسع الإنفاق من العمر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is cited as saying that everything yet to come is near.
rows.anchor: كل ما هو آت قريب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, fa-asaddaq is subjunctive as the answer to a wish, while akuna is jussive as a conditional result: if I give charity, I will be righteous.
rows.anchor: وجزم { أكن } لكونه في معنى جزاء الشرط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Once a person's appointed term arrives, God will not delay it; this ends hope for postponement after death has come and the signs of the next life appear.
rows.anchor: من استجابة دعاء من يسأل تأخير الأجل بعد حلوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase that God knows what people do is either a circumstantial clause or a renewed sentence serving as a reason: do not be distracted, and spend, since God knows and recompenses deeds.
rows.anchor: أو عطف على أول الكلام ويفيد فائدة التعليل

rows.speaker: رواية الفقيه
rows.claim: A report glosses sadaqa as almsgiving and being among the righteous as performing pilgrimage; the author treats the latter as an allusion to one instance.
rows.anchor: أقول الظاهر أن ذيل الحديث من قبيل الإشارة إلى بعض المصاديق

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says someone dying with wealth but unpaid alms, or able to perform pilgrimage but not doing so, asks to return; he identifies righteousness here with pilgrimage, a view also related from Abu Abdillah.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال ما من أحد يموت وكان له مال فلم يؤد زكاته وأطاق الحج فلم يحج إلا سأل الرجعة عند الموت

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar says God has deferred records from which He advances or delays what He wills; on the Night of Decree He sends what will occur through the next year, and what is written in the heavenly book is not delayed.
rows.anchor: قال إن عند الله كتبا موقوفة يقدم منها ما يشاء ويؤخر ما يشاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Day of Assembly is the Resurrection, when people are gathered for judgment; the phrase functions as a time adverb for the prior promise of resurrection and disclosure.
rows.anchor: والمراد بيوم الجمع يوم القيامة الذي يجمع فيه الناس لفصل القضاء بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other verses explain this gathering as God's adjudication and separation of disputes, including 18:99, 45:17, 2:113, and 32:25.
rows.anchor: فالآيات تشير إلى أن جمعهم للقضاء بينهم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines ghubn as secretly undervaluing another party in a transaction and reads the Day of Mutual Loss through profitable or losing exchanges people made in life.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب الغبن أن تبخس صاحبك في معاملة بينك وبينه بضرب من الإخفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first account is attractive but does not fit the apparent reciprocal form of taghabun, which suggests parties acting upon one another.
rows.anchor: وهو معنى حسن غير أنه لا يلائم معنى باب التفاعل الظاهر في فعل البعض في البعض

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A second view says people will discover that things differ from their worldly estimates; the author finds it subtle and sees support in descriptions of unexpected afterlife rewards and disclosures.
rows.anchor: وسئل بعضهم عن يوم التغابن فقال تبدو الأشياء لهم بخلاف مقاديرهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this second account, all gathered people experience mutual loss: believers regret not doing more for the next life, unbelievers did nothing, and both failed to value that Day; the author notes the preceding objection applies too.
rows.anchor: والوجه المشترك بينهما أنهما لم يقدرا اليوم حق قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third account sees leaders and followers in error each causing the other's loss: leaders mislead followers toward worldly life, while followers enable leaders' arrogance.
rows.anchor: أن يعتبر التغابن بين أهل الضلال متبوعيهم وتابعيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A narrated fourth account says each person would have had a Paradise dwelling by obedience and a Fire dwelling by sin; the transfer of dwellings makes believers the winners and unbelievers the losers.
rows.anchor: وهناك وجه رابع وردت به الرواية وهو أن لكل عبد منزلا في الجنة لو أطاع الله لدخله

rows.speaker: بعض المفسرين
rows.claim: Some commentators explain taghabun by the following promise and warning through the phrase about the evil destination; the author says that reading is not very apparent.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض المفسرين بعد إيراد هذا الوجه وقد فسر التغابن قوله ذيلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explanation of the believer who acts righteously and the unbeliever's destination was given repeatedly earlier in the commentary.
rows.anchor: وقوله { ومن يؤمن بالله ويعمل صالحا } إلى قوله { وبئس المصير }

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying that a Paradise entrant is shown the Fire seat they would have occupied by wrongdoing, increasing gratitude, while a Fire entrant sees the Paradise seat they would have had by righteousness, increasing regret.
rows.anchor: ما من عبد يدخل الجنة إلا أري مقعده من النار لو أساء ليزداد شكرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many narrations with this meaning exist in Sunni and Shiite sources, and some were cited earlier under the beginning of 23:1.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى روايات كثيرة من طرق العامة والخاصة وقد تقدم بعضها في تفسير أول سورة المؤمنون

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report defines the Day of Mutual Loss as the day Paradise's people wrongfully gain over Hell's people; it also identifies the meeting, calling, and regret days and says death is slaughtered.
rows.anchor: عن حفص بن غياث عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال يوم التلاق يوم يلتقي أهل السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports interpreting the surah's opening verses through allegiance—faith and unbelief as allegiance, clear proofs as Imams, and light as the Imam—address its inner sense and are not literal exegesis.
rows.anchor: ناظرة إلى بطن الآيات وليست بمفسرة البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A pregnant divorced woman is supported until delivery; if she nurses the child, she is owed nursing wages as part of the child's support paid by the father.
rows.anchor: فلهن عليكم أجر الرضاعة وهو من نفقة الولد التي على الوالد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to consult one another means the man and woman should agree on the child's care by customary fairness, avoiding harm to the father from excessive pay, the mother from too little, and the child from shortened nursing.
rows.anchor: الائتمار بشيء تشاور القوم فيه بحيث يأمر بعضهم فيه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the parents make matters difficult for one another and disagree, the father should hire another woman rather than the child's mother to nurse.
rows.anchor: أي وإن أراد كل منكم من الآخر ما فيه عسر واختلفتم فسترضع الولد امرأة أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person of means should expand support for his divorced wife nursing their child; someone with constrained means supports her according to what he can afford.
rows.anchor: قدر الرزق ضيقه، والإيتاء الإعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God burdens each person only within the capacity He has given, removing hardship from divine obligations including support for a divorced wife.
rows.anchor: لا يكلف الله نفسا إلا بقدر ما أعطاها من القدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise that ease will follow hardship offers reassurance and consolation.
rows.anchor: فيه بشرى وتسلية

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report says the shorter surah called al-Nisaʾ was revealed seven years after the longer al-Baqara surah; the author identifies it as al-Talaq.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن أبي سعيد الخدري قال نزلت سورة النساء القصرى بعد التي في البقرة بسبع سنين

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports divorcing his wife during menstruation; the Prophet ordered him to take her back, wait through another cycle and purification, then divorce before intercourse, identifying this as the prescribed divorce period.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عمر أنه طلق امرأته وهي حائض فذكر ذلك لرسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar's transmitted reading is fi qabli ʿiddatihinna, whereas the written Quranic reading is liʿiddatihinna.
rows.anchor: قراءة ابن عمر وما في المصحف

rows.speaker: ابن سيرين
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin says the passage about God bringing a new matter was revealed concerning Hafsa daughter of Umar, whom the Prophet had divorced once and then taken back.
rows.anchor: قال في حفصة بنت عمر طلقها النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم واحدة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar distinguishes a Sunnah divorce from a divorce of ʿidda and says a divorce contrary to the prescribed Sunnah or ʿidda procedure is invalid.
rows.anchor: عن زرارة عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام أنه قال كل طلاق لا يكون على السنة أو على العدة فليس بشيء

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In Sunnah divorce, the husband waits until menstruation ends, divorces once without intercourse before two witnesses, then leaves her through two more cycles; after three periods they separate, she may remarry him if she wishes, and support, housing, and inheritance continue during the waiting period.
rows.anchor: فإذا أراد الرجل أن يطلق امرأته فينتظر بها حتى تطمث وتطهر فإذا خرجت من طمثها طلقها تطليقة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: In divorce of ʿidda, after a first witnessed divorce without intercourse the husband may return her before the next period, witness the return, and have intercourse; he repeats divorce and return at the next cycles, then a third divorce after the third cycle makes remarriage unlawful until she marries another.
rows.anchor: فلينتظر بها حتى تحيض وتخرج من حيضتها ثم يطلقها تطليقة من غير جماع

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A woman who does not menstruate is divorced by the Sunnah procedure.
rows.anchor: قال مثل هذه تطلق طلاق السنة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu Abdillah says that divorcing a wife three times in one sitting is invalid; anything contrary to the Quran and Sunnah must be returned to them.
rows.anchor: عن صفوان قال سمعت يعني أبا عبد الله وجاء رجل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: The Imam cites the possibility that God may bring about a new matter as support for the invalidity of a one-sitting triple divorce.
rows.anchor: ثم قال ألا تدري { لعل الله يحدث بعد ذلك أمرا }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report from al-Qummi says a husband cannot expel a revocably divorced wife from the home, and she may not leave except for a clear indecency, including adultery, theft against him, or insolent abuse of him.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الفاحشة أن تزني أو تسرق على الرجل

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: A report says a divorced woman remains in her home during the waiting period and displays her adornment to her husband in hope that he may take her back.
rows.anchor: عن وهب بن حفص عن أحدهما عليهما السلام في المطلقة تعتد في بيتها

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says that whoever is granted supplication receives a response, gratitude receives increase, and reliance on God receives sufficiency; it cites 65:3, 14:7, and 40:60.
rows.anchor: من أعطي ثلاثا لم يمنع ثلاثا من أعطي الدعاء أعطي الإجابة

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Asked where God provides unexpectedly for one who is mindful, the Imam answers: in this world.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن مسلم قال سألت أبا عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: سالم بن أبي الجعد
rows.claim: Salim reports the verse was revealed for a man of Ashjaʿ whose son was captured and who faced hardship; after the Prophet advised piety and patience, his son returned freed with goats, and the Prophet said they were his.
rows.anchor: عن سالم بن أبي الجعد قال نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas transmits the Prophet's explanation that piety brings a way out from worldly doubts, death's agonies, and the Day of Resurrection's hardships.
rows.anchor: من طريق عطاء بن يسار عن ابن عباس قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr says the Prophet repeatedly recited the promise of provision for the God-fearing and said it would suffice people if they all followed it; al-Hakim authenticated this report.
rows.anchor: عن أبي ذر قال جعل رسول الله يتلو هذه الآية

rows.speaker: عمران بن حصين
rows.claim: The Prophet says that whoever devotes himself to God is relieved of every burden and provided for unexpectedly, while whoever devotes himself to worldly life is left to it.
rows.anchor: عن عمران بن حصين قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم من انقطع إلى الله كفاه الله كل مؤنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A prophetic report says the strongest person relies on God, the richest trusts what is with God more than what is in his own hand, and the noblest is mindful of God.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رفع الحديث إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says he already explained the meaning of these narrations in his discussion of the verses.
rows.anchor: وقد تقدم في ذيل الكلام على الآيات معنى هذه الروايات

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report sets the waiting period at three months for a woman without menses and for a persistently irregular woman who does not become pure, and at three qurūʾ for one with regular cycles; if irregularity lasts over a month, she should count three months and stop tracking menses.
rows.anchor: عن الحلبي عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report says a pregnant woman's waiting period lasts until delivery, and the husband supports her fairly until then.
rows.anchor: عن محمد بن قيس عن أبي جعفر عليه السلام قال عدة الحامل أن تضع حملها وعليه نفقتها بالمعروف

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: A husband who divorces a pregnant woman supports her until delivery and then pays nursing wages; she has first claim to nurse until weaning unless she accepts the pay of a cheaper nurse.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الصباح الكناني عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام قال إذا طلق الرجل

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: If the husband provides enough to sustain her and clothing, they remain together; otherwise they are separated, according to a report on the constrained provider's duty.
rows.anchor: عن ربعي بن عبد الله والفضيل بن يسار عن أبي عبد الله عليه السلام

rows.speaker: القمي
rows.claim: Al-Qummi says a divorced pregnant woman's waiting ends at delivery, whether she delivers on the day of divorce or after a pregnancy lasting as long as nine months.
rows.anchor: قال المطلقة الحامل أجلها أن تضع ما في بطنها

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن عليه السلام
rows.claim: Abu al-Hasan says any miscarriage whose form shows it was a pregnancy, complete or incomplete, ends the waiting period.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الرحمن بن الحجاج عن أبي الحسن عليه السلام قال سألته عن الحبلى إذا طلقها زوجها فوضعت سقطا

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi confirms that Ali held the waiting period of a widow is the later of two terms and says the pregnant-women rule applies to divorced women.
rows.anchor: عن مغيرة قال قلت للشعبي ما أصدق أن علي بن أبي طالب كان يقول عدة المتوفى عنها زوجها

rows.speaker: فاطمة بنت قيس
rows.claim: Fatima bint Qays reports that after a final divorce the Prophet said she had no maintenance and let her move; she argues the home-retention rule is for revocable divorces, then describes the waiting periods and the requirement of two just witnesses for return.
rows.anchor: أن أبا عمرو بن حفص بن المغيرة خرج مع علي إلى اليمن فأرسل إلى امرأته فاطمة بنت قيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report's legal conclusion is that a husband who takes her back retains two divorces, while a woman whose waiting period ends without return is free to marry whom she chooses.
rows.anchor: فإن راجعها فهي عنده على طلقتين وإن لم يراجعها فإذا انقضت عدتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah consoles the Prophet after the polytheists accuse him of madness, promises reward and honors his great character, forbids compliance and compromise with them, and commands patience for God's judgment.
rows.anchor: تعزي النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم إثر ما رماه المشركون بالجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The surah's overall context is Meccan; the author considers it plausible that the seventeen verses about the garden owners were revealed in Medina.
rows.anchor: ولا يخلو من وجه بالنسبة إلى الآيات السبع عشرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disconnected letter Nun was discussed earlier in the interpretation of al-Shura.
rows.anchor: تقدم الكلام في الحروف المقطعة التي في أوائل السور في تفسير سورة الشورى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qalam is the familiar pen; satar can mean a row of writing, planted trees, or people standing in a row, while the verb means writing line by line.
rows.anchor: الصف من الكتابة، ومن الشجر المغروس ومن القوم الوقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath concerns pen and writing in general, a great divine gift that preserves hidden events and meanings from the barriers of time and distance.
rows.anchor: وظاهر السياق أن المراد بذلك مطلق القلم ومطلق ما يسطرون به وهو المكتوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God taught speech and writing, as stated in 55:3–4 and 96:4–5; the oath honors a gift like other created blessings sworn by in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وقد امتن الله سبحانه على الإنسان بهدايته إليهما وتعليمهما له

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other readings take ma as a verbal noun meaning writing, the pen as the highest pen and its writing as the angels' record, or the writing surface as the Preserved Tablet; the author regards these options as weak.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالقلم القلم الأعلى الذي في الحديث أنه أول ما خلق الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Further options take the plural as honorific, or interpret pen and writing as writers and their written works; the author also calls these possibilities weak.
rows.anchor: واحتمل أن يكون المراد ما يسطرون فيه وهو اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is not mad because of his Lord's favor; the context identifies that favor as prophethood, whose proof excludes mental disorder needed to undermine divine guidance.
rows.anchor: والسياق يؤيد أن المراد بهذه النعمة النبوة فإن دليل النبوة يدفع عن النبي كل اختلال عقلي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view identifies the favor as the Prophet's eloquence, complete reason, good conduct, freedom from defects, and possession of virtues; the author says prophethood is a more decisive proof.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بالنعمة فصاحته صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse and what follows comfort and support the Prophet while refuting the accusation repeated at the surah's end.
rows.anchor: كما أن فيها تكذيبا لقولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's reward for bearing God's message is uncut and will not be wasted; mamnun here derives from cutting off, not reproachful reminders of a favor.
rows.anchor: الممنون من المن بمعنى القطع يقال منه السير منا إذا قطعه وأضعفه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative derives mamnun from reminding someone of a gift, arguing that God's reward is payment for work and therefore carries no reproach; the author rejects this because humans and their deeds belong to God and all reward is grace.
rows.anchor: وربما أخذ المن بمعنى ذكر المنعم إنعامه على المنعم عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khuluq is a settled inward disposition from which actions flow easily; it can be praiseworthy virtue or blameworthy vice, though unqualified use means good character.
rows.anchor: الخلق هو الملكة النفسانية التي تصدر عنها الأفعال بسهولة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib distinguishes khuluq, inward dispositions perceived by insight, from khalq, outward forms and shapes perceived by sight.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب والخلق - بفتح الخاء - والخلق - بضم الخاء - في الأصل واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In context, the Prophet's great character especially means social virtues: steadfastness, patience with abuse, forgiveness, generosity, gentleness, tact, and humility.
rows.anchor: ناظرة إلى أخلاقه الجميلة الاجتماعية المتعلقة بالمعاشرة كالثبات على الحق والصبر على أذى الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether the Prophet or the accusers will prove to be afflicted with madness; the outcome of the mission can become clear in this life, the next, or both.
rows.anchor: فستبصر ويبصرون أيكم المفتون المبتلى بالجنون

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A second grammatical view treats maftun as a verbal noun on a passive-participle pattern and takes bi as meaning in, asking which group is under trial.
rows.anchor: وقيل المفتون مصدر على زنة مفعول كمعقول وميسور ومعسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows best who strays and who is guided because the path belongs to Him and guidance is His affair.
rows.anchor: لأن السبيل سبيله وهو أعلم بمن هو في سبيله ومن ليس فيه وإليه أمر الهداية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition on obeying the deniers follows from their being astray; obedience includes agreeing with them in speech or action.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالطاعة مطلق الموافقة عملا أو قولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The deniers want the Prophet to soften his religion by drawing near to them, so they will reciprocate by compromising theirs; the author understands the desire as covering both parts of the phrase and the fa as elaborating consequence.
rows.anchor: أن تلينهم بالاقتراب منهم في دينك فيلينوك بالاقتراب منك في دينهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One reported proposal was that the Prophet stop mentioning their idols and they would leave him and his Lord alone.
rows.anchor: كما قيل إنهم عرضوا عليه أن يكف عن ذكر آلهتهم فيكفوا عنه وعن ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that great character here means religion or Islam is unsound unless it is referred back to the contextual social virtues just described.
rows.anchor: ومما تقدم يظهر أن ما قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Frequent swearing even over trivial or false matters shows the swearer does not respect what he invokes and, when swearing by God, does not sense God's majesty.
rows.anchor: ولازم كثرة الحلف والإقسام في كل يسير وخطير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mahin means contemptible or base in judgment; other reported senses are malicious, prolific in evil, or a liar.
rows.anchor: والمهين من المهانة بمعنى الحقارة والمراد به حقارة الرأي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hammaz means a persistent fault-finder or taunter; other views make it pointing with eye or gesture, or much backbiting.
rows.anchor: والهماز مبالغة من الهمز والمراد به العياب والطعان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A tale-bearer carries reports between groups to sow discord and corruption.
rows.anchor: والمشاء به هو نقال الحديث من قوم إلى قوم على وجه الإفساد بينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Preventing good means either repeatedly stopping good acts or denying people the good that should reach them; transgression is wrongful violation of limits.
rows.anchor: والمناع للخير كثير المنع لفعل الخير أو للخير الذي ينال أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Athim is someone in whom sin has become settled; sin is a bad deed that holds back good.
rows.anchor: والأثيم هو الذي كثر إثمه حتى استقر فيه من غير زوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Atull is coarse and harsh by nature; reported senses include foul-mannered, unjustly combative, greedy and withholding, or dragging people into imprisonment or punishment.
rows.anchor: والعتل بضمتين هو الفظ الغليظ الطبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zanim may mean rootless, an adopted outsider attached to a group, notorious for baseness, or marked out by evil; these senses are close.
rows.anchor: والزنيم هو الذي لا أصل له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These nine vices describe an enemy of religion who urges the Prophet to obey and compromise; calling him coarse and rootless after the other faults emphasizes two especially severe defects.
rows.anchor: فهذه صفات تسع رذيلة وصف الله بها بعض أعداء الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if his other faults were overlooked, a rude and rootless person should be expelled from human society, not obeyed in word or deed.
rows.anchor: لا ينبغي أن يعبأ بمثله في مجتمع بشري فليطرد ولا يطع في قول ولا يتبع في فعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase about having wealth and sons most likely explains the accumulated vices: he became arrogant and ungrateful instead of improving himself; the author prefers this broader causal reading.
rows.anchor: أي هو يفعل كذا وكذا لأن كان ذا مال وبنين فبطر بذلك وكفر بنعمة الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another reading takes the phrase to mean the Prophet should not obey him merely because he has wealth and sons; the author prefers the preceding explanation.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنه متعلق بقوله السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the revealed signs tales of the ancients supplies a reason for not obeying the denier.
rows.anchor: والآية تجري مجرى التعليل لقوله السابق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Asatir is the plural of ustura, meaning a fanciful or legendary story.
rows.anchor: الأساطير جمع أسطورة وهي القصة الخرافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wasm is marking and khurtum is the nose; calling a human nose a snout, a word used for an elephant or pig, is mockery and a threat for fierce hostility to God and His Messenger.
rows.anchor: وإنما يطلق في الفيل والخنزير تهكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mark on the nose signifies unmistakable humiliation, since the nose signals pride and abasement; the author expects this to occur at the Resurrection and rejects forced interpretations as worldly disgrace.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الوسم على الأنف أريد به نهاية إذلاله بذلة ظاهرة يعرفه بها كل من رآه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden episode is a warning to the Prophet's deniers: like its owners, they arrogantly rely on wealth, children, and apparent causes without gratitude, then face sudden punishment, useless possessions, regret, and repentance too late.
rows.anchor: وعيد لمكذبي النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم الرامين له بالجنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If these verses were revealed with the preceding passage, their warning applies to the deniers generally and recalls the surprise defeat at Badr as worldly proof that apparent causes fail.
rows.anchor: حتى يأتيهم الأجل ويفاجئهم عذاب الآخرة أو عذاب دنيوي من عنده كما فاجأهم يوم بدر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Reports say the passage was revealed during a famine that struck Mecca after the Prophet prayed for years of hardship like Joseph's; the garden owners then parallel Mecca, though the final mutual blame does not fit easily.
rows.anchor: وأما على ما رووا أن الآيات نزلت في القحط والسنة الذي أصاب أهل مكة وقريشا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Balāʾ can mean a test or the affliction itself; sarm is cutting fruit, istithnaʾ is excluding some from a general rule or saying if God wills, and a night visitor is a punishment arriving at night.
rows.anchor: البلاء الاختبار وإصابة المصيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden owners agreed at night to harvest in the morning; not making an exception means they relied on themselves and outward causes without acknowledging God's will.
rows.anchor: وكأنهم ائتمروا وتشاوروا ليلا فعزموا على الصرم صبيحة ليلتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible sense of not making an exception is that they set aside no share of the fruit for the poor.
rows.anchor: أو المعنى قالوا وهم لا يعزلون نصيبا من ثمارهم للفقراء والمساكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A night visitation from God afflicted and surrounded the garden; it became like cut fruitless trees, a dark night after burning, or a barren patch of sand.
rows.anchor: أي بلاء يطوف عليها ويحيط بها ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sarim can mean trees stripped of fruit, a black night, or a piece of sand separated from other sand and unable to grow anything.
rows.anchor: وهو الشجر المقطوع ثمره أو المعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They called to one another at daybreak to go early to the orchard and harvest if they were intent on cutting its fruit; aghdu means go early, with an implicit sense of approaching that explains ala rather than ila.
rows.anchor: فأغدوا أمر بمعنى بكروا مضمن معنى أقبلوا ولذا عدي بعلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They went quietly, consulting in secret to keep poor people from noticing and claiming a share of the harvested fruit.
rows.anchor: والخفت الإخفاء والكتمان، والحرد المنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They set out determined to prevent the poor from receiving anything, confidently planning to harvest it all.
rows.anchor: مقدرين في أنفسهم أنهم سيصرمونها ولا يساهمون المساكين بشيء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On seeing the ruined orchard, they first say they have gone astray from right conduct in trying to harvest and exclude the poor; then they correct themselves: they have been deprived of the crop.
rows.anchor: عن الصواب في غدونا إليها بقصد الصرم ومنع المساكين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view takes their first words to mean that they had lost the way to their orchard; the author instead explains them as moral error.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد إنا لضالون طريق جنتنا وما هي بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their most balanced brother reminded them that he had warned them; the meaning is fairest in judgment, not oldest in age, and his earlier words are omitted for concision.
rows.anchor: أي أعدلهم طريقا وذلك أنه ذكرهم بالحق وإن تبعهم في العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The admonition to glorify God means to declare Him free of partners: their reliance on themselves and worldly causes denied God's sole will, while adding if God wills would affirm that all outcomes depend on Him.
rows.anchor: حيث اعتمدوا على أنفسهم وعلى سائر الأسباب الظاهرية

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes their failure to glorify God as failure to remember and repent for intending to harvest everything and deny the poor; this fits if exception means reserving the poor's share.
rows.anchor: وقيل المراد بتسبيحهم لله ذكر الله تعالى وتوبتهم إليه حيث نووا أن يصرموها ويحرموا المساكين منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their declaration that God is transcendent repudiates the partners they implicitly asserted in their oath and confesses that they wronged themselves; on the other reading it also repents of wronging the poor.
rows.anchor: فهو تسبيح واعتراف بظلمهم على أنفسهم في إثبات الشركاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After recognizing their wrongdoing, they turned toward one another and blamed each other for it.
rows.anchor: أي يلوم بعضهم بعضا على ما ارتكبوه من الظلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They admit exceeding the bounds of servitude by assigning partners to their Lord and hope He will replace the ruined garden with something better because they now turn to Him alone.
rows.anchor: إنا كنا متجاوزين حد العبودية إذ أثبتنا شركاء لربنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Grammatically, al-ʿadhab is a delayed subject and kathālika its preceding predicate; the garden story supplies an example of how punishment comes.
rows.anchor: العذاب مبتدأ مؤخر، وكذلك خبر مقدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People tested by wealth and children may become arrogant, forget God, rely on outward causes, and disobey; sudden punishment wakes them to regret and seek restored blessings too late, as with the garden owners.
rows.anchor: إنما يكون العذاب على ما وصفناه في قصة أصحاب الجنة وهو أن الإنسان يمتحن بالمال والبنين فيطغى مغترا بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Afterlife punishment is greater because it arises from irresistible divine power, offers no escape even through death, surrounds a person completely, and lasts forever unlike worldly trials.
rows.anchor: لأنه ناش عن قهر إلهي لا يقوم له شيء

rows.speaker: الصادق عليه السلام
rows.claim: A report explains Nun as a river in Paradise that God froze into ink; a luminous pen wrote in the luminous Preserved Tablet everything that was and will be until Resurrection.
rows.anchor: عن سفيان بن سعيد الثوري عن الصادق عليه السلام في تفسير الحروف المقطعة في القرآن قال وأما ن فهو نهر في الجنة
